title: Seminole, Oklahoma, and the lead alto who polished his nails
summary: The Holder band worked ballrooms for oil-boom money, and its lead alto would stop playing to polish his nails.

bands.name: T. Holder's Twelve Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Anyway, but then we'd go down to Seminole -- that's between Oklahoma City and Tulsa -- a lot of money, nothing but money, oil and hustlers and everything and money. Everybody spending plenty of money. We made $75.00 a week for three days in 1930. That was a lot of money. So we got a saxophone player that loved Frankie Trumbauer, looked like Frankie Trumbauer, very light skin, looked like Frankie Trumbauer, but he was so -- could play, pretty sound and everything, and we had a lot of hard reed choruses in those days. And we'd get right in the middle of the reed chorus and he's the leader, he just might take his horn down and put it in the stand and started polishing his nails.
I hate to call his name, because he's still playing, you know? He lives out in California (inaudible).

And anyway, he's still alive, you know. But he was weird. So we kept saying, "We got to get a saxophone player." We didn't have but three saxophone players. So we said, "We got to find us a good first saxophone player. We got to have one because this man, you know, he lets us down." And so we go to Tulsa to play a one-nighter in the same place Louis Armstrong played when I met him. I'll tell you how that happened.
